_link.title: I can explain long-term depression, including the structural changes it produces at the neural synapse

toLevel2.answer: The long-lasting weakening of synaptic connections
distractors: The long-lasting strengthening of synaptic connections
The creation of entirely new neurons in the brain
The temporary increase in neurotransmitter release

toLevel2.stem: LTD occurs in synaptic connections between neurons that are what?
distractors: Frequently coactivated
Permanently connected
Newly formed by sprouting

toLevel2.stem: Which of the following is one of the three structural changes produced by LTD?
toLevel2.answer: Decreased number of receptor sites on dendrites
distractors: Increased number of receptor sites on dendrites
Bushier dendrites due to extensive sprouting
Increased number of synaptic connections formed

toLevel2.stem: Which mechanism of synaptic plasticity is primarily involved in LTD?
distractors: Sprouting
Rerouting
Potentiation

toLevel2.stem: How many structural changes does LTD produce at the neural synapse?
distractors: One
Two
Four

toLevel2.stem: Long-term depression involves the weakening of synaptic connections due to infrequent coactivation.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: LTD produces bushier dendrites and an increased number of synaptic connections.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: LTD is the long-lasting {{blank:1}} of synaptic connections between neurons that are not regularly coactivated.

distractors: strengthening
maintenance

toLevel2.stem: The three structural changes of LTD are decreased receptor sites, fewer {{blank:1}} due to pruning, and decreased synaptic connections.

distractors: axons
vesicles

toLevel2.stem: LTD involves {{blank:1}}, which removes unused connections, as its primary mechanism.

distractors: sprouting
rerouting

toLevel3.stem: Why is LTD considered adaptive rather than harmful?
toLevel3.answer: It prevents the brain from maintaining unnecessary connections
distractors: It strengthens all existing connections to improve memory
It creates new connections to replace the ones being lost
It has no adaptive function and is always harmful to the brain

toLevel3.stem: How does LTD explain forgetting information after periods of disuse?
toLevel3.answer: Infrequent use causes synaptic connections to weaken through pruning
distractors: The brain deliberately deletes specific memories to save storage
New neurons replace old ones, overwriting the original information
Forgetting is random and unrelated to any structural neural changes

toLevel3.stem: How does a decreased number of receptor sites contribute to weaker synaptic connections?
toLevel3.answer: Fewer receptor sites mean less neurotransmitter can bind
distractors: Fewer receptor sites mean more neurotransmitter can bind
Receptor sites have no relationship to connection strength
Decreased receptor sites cause the connection to strengthen

toLevel3.stem: How does LTD differ from LTP in terms of the structural changes it produces?
toLevel3.answer: LTD decreases receptor sites and prunes dendrites; LTP increases them
distractors: Both LTD and LTP produce identical structural changes at synapses
LTD increases receptor sites; LTP decreases receptor sites on dendrites
Neither LTD nor LTP involves any structural changes at the synapse

toLevel3.stem: Why does LTD result from infrequent stimulation rather than frequent stimulation?
toLevel3.answer: Without regular use, connections are not maintained and weaken
distractors: Infrequent stimulation strengthens connections more than frequent use
The brain strengthens all connections regardless of how often they fire
Frequent stimulation causes connections to weaken through overuse

toLevel3.stem: How does LTD free resources for more relevant memory traces?
toLevel3.answer: Removing unused connections allows resources to support active pathways
distractors: LTD strengthens all connections equally to share resources more fairly
LTD creates new neurons that take over from the weakened connections
Resources are unlimited in the brain so LTD has no resource function

toLevel3.stem: LTD is adaptive because it prevents the brain from maintaining unnecessary connections, freeing resources for more relevant memory traces.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: LTD explains forgetting because infrequent use causes synaptic connections to {{blank:1}} through the process of pruning.

distractors: strengthen
stabilise

toLevel3.stem: LTD is adaptive because removing unused connections allows the brain to allocate resources to more {{blank:1}} memory traces.

distractors: irrelevant
identical

toLevel3.stem: A decreased number of receptor sites means less {{blank:1}} can bind, making the synaptic connection weaker.

distractors: electrical charge
synaptic vesicle

toLevel4.stem: A student studied Indonesian in Year 8 but stopped practising for five years and now cannot recall most vocabulary. Which process best explains this?
toLevel4.answer: LTD weakened the relevant synaptic connections through pruning
distractors: LTP strengthened the connections, making them harder to access
New neurons replaced the Indonesian vocabulary with other content
The vocabulary was never stored in synaptic connections at all

toLevel4.stem: A VCE exam asks students to name the structural changes produced by LTD. Which response would earn full marks?
toLevel4.answer: Decreased receptor sites, fewer dendrites, and decreased synaptic connections
distractors: Increased receptor sites, bushier dendrites, and more synaptic connections
Decreased receptor sites only, with no other structural changes occurring
Fewer dendrites and increased receptor sites with unchanged connections

toLevel4.stem: Maya used to play netball competitively but stopped for three years. She now finds her skills have declined significantly. Which explanation best applies LTD?
toLevel4.answer: Infrequent use caused pruning of the relevant motor pathway connections
distractors: Frequent practice during the break strengthened irrelevant connections
New neurons were created that overwrote her original netball skill memory
Her motor pathways were physically damaged by the absence of all practice

toLevel4.stem: A student writes: 'LTD makes connections weaker.' A teacher asks for more specific structural detail. Which response best applies?
toLevel4.answer: Receptor sites decrease, dendrites are pruned, and synaptic connections reduce
distractors: Neurons are destroyed and replaced with entirely new unconnected neurons
The synaptic gap widens and neurotransmitters can no longer cross the space
Axon terminals shrink and stop producing any neurochemicals for the synapse

toLevel4.stem: Oliver has not revised his Year 10 chemistry knowledge for two years. He finds he can barely remember any formulas. How does LTD explain this?
toLevel4.answer: The chemistry-related connections weakened due to infrequent coactivation
distractors: LTP strengthened the chemistry pathways but made them inaccessible
The formulas were moved to a different brain region and cannot be found
His brain replaced chemistry neurons with neurons for other subjects

toLevel4.stem: A researcher examines brain tissue from a person who abandoned piano practice years ago. Which finding would be most consistent with LTD?
toLevel4.answer: Fewer dendrites and reduced receptor sites in relevant motor regions
distractors: Bushier dendrites and increased receptor sites in motor cortex areas
No structural changes of any kind in the relevant brain region tissue
Increased synaptic connections throughout the entire cerebral cortex

toLevel4.stem: A student argues that LTD is harmful because it causes forgetting. How should this be reframed using knowledge of LTD's adaptive function?
toLevel4.answer: LTD frees resources by removing unnecessary connections for more relevant ones
distractors: LTD is indeed harmful and has no adaptive function in the brain at all
LTD only occurs in damaged brains and is not a normal brain process
LTD strengthens connections, so the student's premise is already wrong

toLevel4.stem: The student who cannot recall Indonesian vocabulary after five years without practice has experienced LTD, which {{blank:1}} the relevant synaptic connections through {{blank:2}}.

distractors: strengthened
maintained
sprouting
rerouting

toLevel4.stem: Maya's decline in netball skills is explained by LTD because infrequent use caused {{blank:1}} of the motor pathway connections.

distractors: sprouting
potentiation

toLevel4.stem: A student who writes that LTD 'makes connections weaker' should add that the specific changes are decreased receptor sites, fewer dendrites, and decreased {{blank:1}}.

distractors: electrical impulses
neuron cell bodies

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that LTD is harmful because it causes people to forget important information. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Oversimplified; LTD is adaptive because it removes unnecessary connections
distractors: Correct; LTD is always harmful and serves no useful purpose at all
Correct; forgetting is always negative and should be prevented entirely
Incorrect; LTD does not cause any forgetting under any circumstances

toLevel5.stem: Dr Chen argues that simply saying 'connections weaken' is sufficient to describe LTD. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Insufficient; specific structural changes must be named for full exam marks
distractors: Correct; no further detail is needed beyond saying connections weaken
Correct; examiners never require specific structural detail about LTD
Insufficient; but only one structural change needs to be identified

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that LTD destroys neurons entirely. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; LTD weakens connections through pruning, not neuron destruction
distractors: Correct; LTD completely destroys neurons that are no longer being used
Correct; pruning means the entire neuron is removed from the brain
Incorrect; LTD actually strengthens neurons rather than weakening them

toLevel5.stem: Emma argues that LTD means a person can never relearn a forgotten skill. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; resumed practice can trigger LTP to restrengthen weakened connections
distractors: Correct; once LTD occurs, the connections are permanently and irreversibly lost
Correct; the brain cannot form new connections in areas where LTD has occurred
Incorrect; LTD does not affect skill retention in any way and is irrelevant

toLevel5.stem: A student writes that LTD produces 'fewer neurons.' Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; LTD changes connections between neurons, not the number of neurons
distractors: Correct; LTD reduces the total number of neurons in the affected brain area
Correct; pruning removes entire neurons from the brain during the process
Incorrect; LTD actually increases the number of neurons in the brain region

toLevel5.stem: Marcus argues that LTD and forgetting are the same thing. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Oversimplified; LTD is one neural mechanism that contributes to forgetting
distractors: Correct; LTD and forgetting are identical interchangeable concepts always
Incorrect; LTD has no connection to forgetting or memory loss at all
Correct; there is no difference between the two terms in psychology

toLevel5.stem: A researcher claims that LTD only occurs during sleep. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; LTD occurs when connections are infrequently used, regardless of sleep
distractors: Correct; synaptic changes can only occur during sleep and rest periods
Correct; the brain only prunes connections while a person is sleeping
Incorrect; LTD only occurs during periods of intense waking brain activity

toLevel5.stem: A student suggests that preventing all LTD would improve memory. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Problematic; without LTD the brain would maintain unnecessary connections
distractors: Correct; preventing LTD would ensure all memories are retained permanently
Correct; LTD serves no useful function and preventing it would be beneficial
Problematic; but only because LTD cannot actually be prevented by any means

toLevel5.stem: The claim that LTD destroys neurons is {{blank:1}} because LTD weakens {{blank:2}} through pruning, not the neurons themselves.

distractors: correct
plausible
neurons
receptors

toLevel5.stem: The claim that LTD means a skill can never be relearned is {{blank:1}} because resumed practice can trigger {{blank:2}} to restrengthen weakened connections.

distractors: correct
plausible
LTD
pruning
